scope: Conditional bounded audit under the user-specified accepted manuscript inputs; no certification of the homogeneous replacement proof.

statement_checks.location: Opening setup and contextual analytic-barrier claim
checks: The standing manuscript conventions specify connected compact complex X of positive dimension without boundary. This supplies finite suprema and uniform constants; no noncompact extension is claimed.
The displayed strict analytic barrier is an explicit hypothesis. Analytic poles form a proper analytic set because rho is genuine; smoothness off that set is separately supplied.
In the manuscript, big means there is a genuine q with theta+ddc q>=kappa0 omega for some kappa0>0. It does not mean positive numerical volume or a nef-volume criterion.

With manuscript ddc=i/(2pi)partial barpartial, apply Demailly's Theorem 14.12 to phi=q/2 and gamma=kappa0 omega-theta. Its approximants phi_m give q_m=2phi_m, so ddc q_m>=gamma-epsilon_m omega and q_m has logarithmic analytic singularities. The current being regularized is the closed ddc q, not theta+ddc q.

The source's glued Bergman construction is smooth wherever its positive weighted sum is nonzero. Its local coherent ideals agree across charts, so the zero set is analytic. Thus the chosen approximant is smooth off its analytic pole set; this is not inferred from a bounded-remainder definition alone.

Choose m with epsilon_m<kappa0/2 and set rho=q_m. It is genuine, has the needed poles/smoothness, and theta+ddc rho>=kappa0 omega/2. Closedness of gamma, theta, or omega is not needed. Exact external evidence is recorded separately.
statement_checks.normalization_note: Expands the harmless operator-normalization conversion in the initial record; no issue in the submitted proof.

checks: A genuine quasi-psh rho has finite upper bound on compact X; h has finite minimum. Subtraction of a finite constant makes rho+2<=h without changing ddc rho.
rho+2 is a genuine theta-psh competitor, so the accepted elementary envelope construction gives genuine canonical p and rho+2<=p<=h everywhere.
On every compact neighborhood off Z, rho is smooth and bounded below, whereas h is bounded above. Thus p is finite and uniformly bounded on that neighborhood before continuity is known.
p is quasi-psh since ddc p>=-theta and theta is smooth. As a genuine quasi-psh function on compact X, p is in L1; global boundedness below is not asserted.

statement_checks.location: Regularization paragraph — exact Demailly input and constants
checks: The manuscript convention is ddc=i/(2pi)partial barpartial, while Demailly uses i/pi. The literal substitution is T_D=ddc p, alpha_D=0, psi_D=p/2 and gamma=-theta. T_D and alpha_D are closed; gamma is merely a continuous real lower form in Theorem 4.1.

Choose a smooth curvature comparison form A omega with A>0 sufficiently large. Compactness bounds the negative Chern bisectional curvature, in particular on the source's required orthogonal pairs. This auxiliary form is unrelated to semipositivity of theta.

The source's equations (3.1)-(3.2) are positive normalized radial formal-exph averages. Changing variables produces a smooth kernel for positive radius, so averaging an L1 potential is finite and smooth, even when its values are minus infinity on a pluripolar set.

Theorem 4.1 is stated for general quasi-psh psi, not bounded psi. Its full base-fiber lower bound has a fixed mixed error C|zeta||eta| and vertical error C|eta|^2, not just a horizontal Hessian estimate.

The proof of Proposition 3.8 estimates remainders by local integrals of the potential and its positive corrected Hessian. The mean-value/Lelong estimates on pp.10-12 allow logarithmic averaged growth and O(t^-2) scaled Hessian integrals. They do not require a finite global infimum or L-infinity norm.

The constants may depend on this fixed p, its finite local L1 bounds, its smooth lower bound and the fixed geometry. They are uniform in x and small t, independent of c and delta; no uniform estimate over a family of envelopes is needed.

With K0 from the source, lambda=t*d/dt(R_t p+K0 t^2) is nonnegative and increasing. The corrected averages are logarithmically convex, increase with t, and converge to the canonical p; hence R_t p+K0 t^2>=p.

Pointwise convergence follows also from Remark 4.6 comparing with ordinary radial convolution up to O(t^2). Upper semicontinuity and the psh local correction identify the limit with the canonical representative, including unbounded potentials.

Linearity gives Psi_D=R_t p/2 and ddc_D Psi_D=ddc_here R_t p. Taking K0=2K0,D yields lambda_here=2lambda_D, so the curvature coefficient is rescaled to A_D/2 and other fixed constants are renamed. This exactly preserves the displayed form of the proof's estimates; no theta coefficient is altered.
statement_checks.normalization_note: Expands the harmless operator-normalization conversion in the initial record; no issue in the submitted proof.

statement_checks.location: Regularization paragraph — correction and mixed-error absorption
checks: Take K>=K0 with K>0 and write F(z,t)=R_t p+Kt^2+Kt. Its logarithmic derivative is lambda_tilde=lambda+2(K-K0)t^2+Kt>=lambda.
The second logarithmic derivative of F is d(lambda)/d(log t)+4(K-K0)t^2+Kt>0, so subtracting c log t preserves strict convexity in log t.
The Hessian of K|w| contributes a positive vertical term proportional to K|eta|^2/(4t). Young's inequality bounds C|zeta||eta| by C' t|zeta|^2 plus part of that vertical contribution.
For sufficiently small t the remaining positive vertical term absorbs C|eta|^2. K|w|^2 only adds a nonnegative vertical term.
The resulting full lower bound is -theta-(A lambda+epsilon0(t)+C't)omega on base directions. Replacing lambda by the larger lambda_tilde weakens the estimate in the valid direction.
Take an increasing nonnegative majorant epsilon(t) of epsilon0(t)+C't, tending to zero. The procedure uses the source's fixed constants and neither semipositivity of theta nor boundedness below of p.
The source's Remark 4.7 uses a different correction Psi+|w| with derivative lambda+t-2K0t^2. It is not identified with F; the larger correction used here has been checked directly.

statement_checks.location: Regularization paragraph — minimizing radii and local minimum principle
checks: For fixed c>0 and small delta, the objective is at least p-K(delta^2+delta)-c log(t/delta). On a fixed compact neighborhood off Z, the first term has a uniform lower bound.

At t=delta the objective is R_delta p<=R_delta h, uniformly bounded above. Hence all local minimizers lie in one compact interval [b,delta] with b>0, for these fixed parameters. No information about p on kernel supports beyond the global smoothing inequality is required.

Smoothness for positive radius, compactness of that interval, and strict logarithmic convexity give a unique minimizing radius, continuous in the base point. The minimum value is finite and continuous locally off Z.
At an interior minimizing radius lambda_tilde=c; at the upper cap lambda_tilde<=c, since the left derivative of the objective there is nonpositive.

For any small eta>0, continuity of the minimizer and of lambda_tilde allows a fixed radial interval around nearby minimizers whose upper endpoint has lambda_tilde<c+eta. Monotonicity bounds it on the entire interval.
If the minimizer is the cap, the infimum over the open interval ending at delta equals its closed-cap minimum by continuity. The general Kiselman principle does not require interior attainment.

Write w=exp(tau) on a product of a coordinate ball and a strip. This product is pseudoconvex, has connected tube fibers, and the objective is independent of Im(tau); the logarithmic penalty is pluriharmonic.
Freeze B(z)=theta(z)+(A(c+eta)+epsilon(delta))omega(z). For any e>0 a quadratic q with ddc q=B(z0)+e beta makes the full objective plus q psh on a sufficiently small base ball.

Kiselman's minimum principle applies to this finite fiber infimum. Comparing B(z0) with B(z), covering the base neighborhoods, and letting e and then eta tend to zero gives theta+ddc Phi>=-(Ac+epsilon(delta))omega locally throughout X minus Z.
This repeats the audited lemma's method on compact neighborhoods where p is bounded; no assertion of its globally bounded conclusion for this p has been assumed.
Evaluating at t=delta makes both polynomial corrections and the logarithmic penalty zero, giving Phi<=R_delta p.
Positivity of the same averaging kernel and p<=h imply R_delta p<=R_delta h.
R_delta h is smooth and bounded for fixed delta, so Phi has a uniform upper bound near the entire analytic set Z. The bound applies on the domain X minus Z, as needed for removal.

statement_checks.location: Extension paragraph — removable singularities with the precise lower form
checks: Put e0=Ac+epsilon(delta) and B=theta+e0 omega. On X minus Z, ddc Phi>=-B.
On a fixed coordinate region let beta be a constant positive Euclidean form. For any eta>0, around any center z0 choose a ball on which -eta beta<=B(z)-B(z0)<=eta beta.

Choose a real quadratic q with ddc q=B(z0)+eta beta. Then Phi+q is psh off Z and locally bounded above. The allowed analytic-set removable singularity theorem extends it by limsup from the complement.

Subtract q. The extension equals limsup of Phi from the complement because q is continuous, so extensions using different centers, corrections, or eta agree. It is a genuine global quasi-psh function since Phi is finite off the proper set Z.
The corrected extension satisfies ddc Phi>=-B(z0)-eta beta>=-B(z)-2eta beta on that ball. For each eta these balls cover the fixed coordinate region, and current positivity is local.
Thus ddc Phi+B+2eta beta>=0 throughout the region. Let eta decrease to zero in pairings with positive test forms. This gives ddc Phi+B>=0 exactly, including on Z.

This argument uses potentials only for constant coefficient forms, and never assumes a local potential for nonclosed theta. The shrinking balls cause no gap because the inequality is patched for each fixed eta before taking the limit.
The upper bound Phi<=R_delta h survives the limsup extension since R_delta h is continuous.

statement_checks.location: Extension paragraph — lower comparison with the barrier
checks: For every t<=delta, R_t p+Kt^2>=p, Kt>=0, and -c log(t/delta)>=0. Taking the infimum gives Phi>=p-K(delta^2+delta) off Z.
Take delta small enough that K(delta^2+delta)<=1. The initial envelope inequality then gives Phi>=rho+1 off Z.
On Z the barrier equals minus infinity, so rho<=Phi there as an extended-real inequality regardless of whether Phi is finite. Thus rho<=Phi everywhere.

statement_checks.location: Parameter paragraph — m, c, and s
checks: Kernel support lies within distance C t of the base point for all small t, and the kernel is positive with integral one. Hence |R_t h-h| is bounded by the uniform continuity modulus of h at Ct.
Taking the supremum over 0<t<=delta gives finite nonnegative m(delta) tending to zero. This does not assume h is differentiable.
c=m(delta)+epsilon(delta)+delta is positive, tends to zero, and dominates m(delta), epsilon(delta), and delta.

With A>=0 and kappa>0, s=(Ac+epsilon(delta))/kappa is nonnegative, tends to zero, and satisfies s<=((A+1)/kappa)c and s kappa=Ac+epsilon(delta). We may keep A>0 to avoid any zero-times-minus-infinity notation.
The affine-current identity is theta+ddc v=[theta+ddc Phi+s(theta+ddc rho)]/(1+s). It holds for nonclosed theta.
Its numerator is at least (-(Ac+epsilon(delta))+s kappa)omega=0, so v is theta-psh.
Both summands are genuine quasi-psh, bounded above, and finite off Z. Their positive affine combination is genuine, L1, and has the canonical quasi-psh representative.
Since rho<=Phi and s>=0, v<=Phi<=R_delta h<=h+m(delta), with the same valid extended-real inequality at poles.
Subtracting m(delta) leaves the theta-psh condition unchanged and produces a genuine envelope competitor. Hence v-m(delta)<=p, or v<=p+m(delta), everywhere.
Only the envelope definition is used for this comparison; there is no stability theorem, contact theorem, or Monge-Ampere mass estimate.

statement_checks.location: Compact-set paragraph — control of Phi minus p
checks: On L compactly contained in X minus Z, p and rho are finite and p-rho<=sup_L h-inf_L rho<infinity.
Multiplying the definition of v by 1+s gives exactly Phi-p=(1+s)(v-p)+s(p-rho). The last term has a plus sign.
Use v-p<=m(delta), bounded 1+s, and s=O(c) to get Phi-p<=C_L c. Constants depend on L and the fixed data, not delta or the base point in L.
The lower bound Phi-p>=-K(delta^2+delta) remains available; neither bound presupposes continuity of p.
At the previously established minimizer t, rearrange its defining equality: -c log(t/delta)=Phi-(R_t p+Kt^2)-Kt+K(delta^2+delta).
Use R_t p+Kt^2>=p and -Kt<=0 to obtain -c log(t/delta)<=Phi-p+K(delta^2+delta).
For delta<1, delta^2+delta<=2delta<=2c. The preceding compact-set estimate bounds the right hand side by another C_L c.
Divide by c>0 to obtain log(delta/t)<=C_L. Thus t>=a_L delta with a_L=exp(-C_L)>0, decreased to at most one if necessary. It is fixed for L and independent of delta.
No uniform global lower bound for minimizing radii near Z is claimed or needed.

statement_checks.location: Compact-set paragraph — uniform smoothing convergence and continuity
checks: Monotonicity and a_L delta<=t give R_(a_L delta)p+K(a_L delta)^2<=R_t p+Kt^2.
The minimum identity gives R_t p+Kt^2=Phi+Kdelta^2+Kdelta-Kt+c log(t/delta)<=Phi+Kdelta^2+Kdelta.
Dropping the nonnegative term K(a_L delta)^2 proves the asserted upper bound; the source's monotone lower bound gives R_(a_L delta)p>=p-K(a_L delta)^2.
Combine with Phi-p<=C_L c to obtain sup_L |R_(a_L delta)p-p|<=C'_L c, which tends to zero.
Each R_(a_L delta)p is smooth for positive radius by its L1 kernel representation. A sequence delta decreasing to zero yields a uniform limit of continuous functions on L.
Take compact neighborhoods inside X minus Z to obtain continuity at every point there. This proves the first assertion without contact support and without a global smoothing gradient bound.

statement_checks.location: Contact paragraph — open ball and conditional replacement
checks: For x in {p<h} minus Z, continuity of p and h off Z gives a neighborhood with positive obstacle slack; choose a coordinate ball whose closure lies there.
p is continuous on that closed ball and theta-psh inside, so p restricted to the boundary is continuous admissible boundary data.

The exact conditional theorem gives a continuous theta-psh H on the closed ball with the same boundary, homogeneous bounded local MA in the interior, and domination of every continuous theta-psh competitor with boundary below the data.

Taking p itself as competitor gives H>=p. No comparison for unbounded competitors or different backgrounds is used. The contraction and smooth-boundary Lipschitz assertions of the prerequisite are not needed.
The prerequisite's proof and the outcome of its separate audit local_homogeneous_dirichlet_01 are not certified or assumed to have passed by this audit.

statement_checks.location: Obstacle-slack paragraph — uniform scalar upper bound
checks: Fix one chart around x before varying r. Tracing theta+ddc H>=0 against the Euclidean metric gives the distributional inequality Delta H>=-C, with C depending only on a fixed upper bound for the trace of smooth theta on the chart.
Set S_r=sup_boundary(B_r) p and q_r=S_r+C'(r^2-|z-x|^2). In the real Euclidean convention Delta |z-x|^2=4n; choose C'>=C/(4n), adjusted for the fixed ddc normalization if needed.
Delta(H-q_r)>=0, while H-q_r<=0 on the boundary. The scalar subharmonic maximum principle applies to the continuous H, giving H<=q_r<=S_r+C'r^2.
C' is independent of r and H. Continuity of p at x gives S_r+C'r^2 tending to p(x); continuity of h gives inf_Br h tending to h(x).
If d=h(x)-p(x)>0, shrink so S_r+C'r^2<p(x)+d/3 and inf_Br h>h(x)-d/3. Then H<h on the ball, and in particular H<=h, while the closure remains away from Z.
This uses only a scalar trace and scalar maximum principle; it does not invoke a theta potential or a nonclosed Monge-Ampere comparison theorem.
For a>0, continuity of H-p on the closed ball and its zero boundary values give H-a
Define q_a=max(p,H-a) inside and p outside. It is p on a neighborhood of the boundary and theta-psh elsewhere by the accepted max closure for this same theta.
Let q equal H inside and p outside. It is well defined and continuous near the boundary because boundary values agree; it equals the canonical p away from the ball.
Since H>=p inside, H-a<=q_a<=H there. Thus 0<=q-q_a<=a inside and q_a=q=p outside; the differences are supported off Z.

As a decreases to zero the convergence is uniformly controlled near and inside the closed ball, and is unchanged elsewhere. In particular it is local L1 convergence, so theta+ddc q>=0 follows by passing to currents.

The resulting pasted representative is quasi-psh and canonical: it is the continuous representative around the closed ball and equals p on the exterior. Alternatively the same local uniform limit after quadratic correction is psh.
Both H and p are at most h in their respective regions, so q<=h globally; q is genuine since it is finite off Z. It is therefore a valid envelope competitor.
q>=p by H>=p, while the definition of p gives q<=p. Consequently q=p everywhere and p=H on B_r.
None of these operations requires closedness of theta. A bare piecewise gluing without the max/collar argument would not suffice, but the submitted proof supplies that argument.

statement_checks.location: Final contact paragraph — locality and extended measure
checks: p=H on B_r and both functions are locally bounded there. The conditional homogeneous equation and locality of the accepted local bounded product give MA_theta(p)(B_r)=0.
Such balls cover U={p<h} minus Z. Since the manifold is second countable, choose a countable subcover; countable subadditivity gives MA_theta(p)(U)=0 even when the total measure is infinite.

The accepted extended measure agrees with the bounded local measure off Z and charges no pluripolar set. Z is analytic and is also contained in the pole set of the global quasi-psh rho, hence pluripolar.
The set {p<h} is Borel (indeed p-h is upper semicontinuous). Its intersection with Z has zero extended measure. Together with U this yields the displayed restricted measure equal to zero on all X.
No finite-total-mass subtraction, dominated convergence of masses, BMP, or PVP is used.

statement_checks.location: Closing scope and full hypothesis-use audit
checks: The argument treats continuous finite obstacles only. No transition to quasi-continuous unbounded obstacles is asserted.
Compactness enters normalization, L1 integrability, uniform geometry/kernel constants, and uniform continuity of h. The standing manuscript supplies it explicitly.
Theta smoothness supplies the lower-form regularity, local freezing and uniform scalar trace bound; its closedness and semipositivity are never used.

Strictness kappa>0 absorbs Ac+epsilon(delta) by the affine barrier correction. Local boundedness of rho off Z controls p and p-rho on compact sets; analyticity of Z permits removal and pluripolar noncharging.
The independently asserted smoothness of rho off Z is stronger than the local boundedness needed for these estimates and is harmless; it is available from the classical construction.
Bigness need not be used again after the explicit strict barrier has been supplied. Its contextual implication has been separately checked with gamma=kappa0 omega-theta.
The only local homogeneous replacement properties used are continuous solvability, the same boundary, homogeneous MA, and domination of continuous competitors, all expressly accepted conditionally.
The conclusion is conditional on that prerequisite and the stated accepted manuscript inputs. It is not a formal verification, novelty certification, or certification of the replacement proof.

reference_checks.location: Opening contextual claim: bigness supplies a strict analytic barrier
reference_checks.referenced_statement: Demailly analytic regularization theorem for quasi-plurisubharmonic functions with a smooth possibly nonclosed lower bound: if psi is quasi-plurisubharmonic on a compact Hermitian manifold and dd^c psi >= gamma for a continuous real (1,1)-form gamma, there are quasi-plurisubharmonic psi_m with analytic singularities, smooth off their analytic pole sets, such that dd^c psi_m >= gamma-epsilon_m omega and epsilon_m tends to zero. Consequently if theta is smooth possibly nonclosed and theta+dd^c psi >= kappa omega, one obtains an analytic singularity potential rho with theta+dd^c rho >= kappa/2 omega.

results.title: Kähler-Einstein metrics on stable varieties and log canonical pairs
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, $dV$ some volume form, $D=\sum a_{i}D_{i}$ a $\mathbb{R}$-divisor with coefficients in $(-\infty,1]$ and defining sections $s_{i}$, $E=\sum c_{\alpha}E_{\alpha}$ an effective $\mathbb{R}$-divisor such that $D_{red}+E$ has snc support, and $\theta$ a semipositive form with $\int_{X}\theta^{n}>0$ such that $\{\theta\}-c_{1}(E)$ is a Kähler class. Then the $\theta$-psh function $\varphi$ with full Monge-Ampère mass, which is a solution of



$\langle(\theta+dd^{c}\phi)^{n}\rangle=\frac{e^{\varphi}dV}{\prod_{i}|s_{i}|^{2a_{j}}}$



is smooth outside of $\mathrm{Supp}(D)\cup\mathrm{Supp}(E)$.

results.title: Optimal $L^2$ Extensions of Openness Type
Envelopes with Prescribed Singularities
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and $\theta,\gamma$ two closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ such that $[\theta]$ is big, $[\gamma]$ is pseudoeffective, and $[\theta-\gamma]$ is nef. Suppose also that $u\in C^{\infty}(X)$ and $\psi\in PSH(X,\gamma)$ with analytic singularities. Then if either:


(1)

$[\theta-\gamma]$ is big, or



(2)

$\int_{X}\langle(\gamma+\sqrt{-1}\partial\overline{\partial}\psi)^{n}\rangle>0,$



we have that $P_{[\psi]}(u)\in C^{1,1}_{loc}(X\setminus Y)$, where $Y\subset X$ is a proper analytic subset given either by $Y=E_{nK}(\theta-\gamma)\cup\mathrm{Sing}(\psi)$ in case $(1)$, or by $Y=\mu(E_{nK}(\widetilde{\gamma}))\cup\mathrm{Sing}(\psi)$ in case $(2)$ (where $\widetilde{\gamma}$ and $\mu$ are defined in (2.1) below).

reference_checks.arxiv_comparison: The returned Kähler-Einstein and closed-Kähler envelope statements do not match. The equisingular approximation statement in arXiv:2202.04791, Theorem 2.5, asserts smoothness off an analytic set but not the required analytic singularity type; it is not used as a substitute.
reference_checks.source: Demailly, Analytic Methods in Algebraic Geometry, July 2011, Section 14.B, equations (14.6)-(14.8), the gluing on p.142, and Theorem 14.12(c), pp.142-143.
reference_checks.context_expansion: The theorem concerns an almost psh scalar potential on any compact complex manifold with an arbitrary continuous real lower form gamma; gamma need not be closed. The constructed logarithmic analytic singularities are comparable to finite holomorphic generator norms. Smoothness off their poles is checked from the positive smooth weighted Bergman sum, not inferred merely from the bounded remainder terminology.
reference_checks.application: For theta+ddc q>=kappa0 omega in the manuscript normalization, put phi_D=q/2 and gamma=kappa0 omega-theta. The source gives phi_m and ddc_D phi_m>=gamma-epsilon_m omega. Set rho=2phi_m and take epsilon_m<kappa0/2. Then theta+ddc rho>=kappa0 omega/2, with a proper analytic pole set and smoothness on its complement.

results.title: A generalization of Nadel vanishing theorem
results.theorem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a complex manifold equipped with a Hermitian metric $\omega$, and $\Omega\Subset X$ be an open subset.
Assume that $T=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\mathrm{i}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi$
is a closed $(1,1)$-current on $X$,
where $\widetilde{T}$ is a smooth real $(1,1)$-form and $\varphi$ is a quasi-plurisubharmonic function.
Let $\gamma$ be a continuous real $(1,1)$-form such that $T\geqslant\gamma$. Suppose that the Chern curvature tensor of $TX$ satisfies



$\left(\mathrm{i}\Theta_{T_{X}}+\theta\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{T_{X}}\right)\left(\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2},\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2}\right)\geqslant 0\quad\forall\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\in T_{X}~{}\text{with}~{}\langle\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\rangle=0$



for some continuous nonnegative $(1,1)$-form $\theta$ on $X$.
Then there is a family of closed $(1,1)$-currents $T_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\mathrm{i}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}$ on $X$ such that


(i)

$\varphi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\bar{\Omega}$, smooth on $X\backslash E_{\sigma}(T)$, increasing with respect to $\varsigma$ and $\varepsilon$ on $\Omega$, and converges to $\varphi$ on $\Omega$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$,



(ii)

$T_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}\geqslant\gamma-\varsigma\theta-\delta_{\varepsilon}\omega$ on $\Omega$,



where $E_{\varsigma}(T)=\left\{x\in X;\nu(T,x)\geqslant\varsigma\right\}$, $\varsigma>0$, is the $\varsigma$-upperlevel set of Lelong numbers, and $\{\delta_{\varepsilon}\}$ is an increasing family of positive numbers such that $\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\delta_{\varepsilon}=0$.

results.title: Optimal $L^2$ extension of sections from subvarieties in weakly pseudoconvex manifolds
results.theorem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a complex manifold equipped with a Hermitian
metric $\omega$, and Ω⊂⊂X\Omega\subset\subset X be an open subset.
Assume that $T=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\sqrt{-1}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi$ is a closed $(1,1)$-current on $X$,
where $\widetilde{T}$ is a smooth real $(1,1)$-form and $\varphi$ is
a quasi-plurisubharmonic function. Let $\gamma$ be a continuous real
$(1,1)$-form such that $T\geq\gamma$. Suppose that the Chern
curvature tensor of $T_{X}$ satisfies



$(\sqrt{-1}\Theta_{T_{X}}+\varpi\otimes\mathrm{Id}_{T_{X}})(\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2},\kappa_{1}\otimes\kappa_{2})\geq 0\quad(\forall\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\in T_{X}\text{ with }\langle\kappa_{1},\kappa_{2}\rangle=0)$



for some continuous nonnegative
$(1,1)$-form $\varpi$ on $X$. Then there is a family of closed
$(1,1)$-currents $T_{\varsigma,\rho}=\widetilde{T}+\frac{\sqrt{-1}}{\pi}\partial\bar{\partial}\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}$ defined
on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$ ($\varsigma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\rho\in(0,\rho_{1})$ for some
positive number $\rho_{1}$) independent of $\gamma$, such that


$(i)$

$\varphi_{\varsigma,\rho}$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$,
smooth on $\Omega\setminus E_{\varsigma}(T)$, increasing with respect to
$\varsigma$ and $\rho$ on $\Omega$, and converges to $\varphi$ on
$\Omega$ as $\rho\rightarrow 0$,



$(ii)$

$T_{\varsigma,\rho}\geq\gamma-\varsigma\varpi-\delta_{\rho}\omega$ on $\Omega$,



where $E_{\varsigma}(T):=\{x\in X:\,\nu(T,x)\geq\varsigma\}$
$(\varsigma>0)$ is the $\varsigma$-upperlevel set of Lelong numbers,
and $\{\delta_{\rho}\}$ is an increasing family of positive numbers
such that $\lim\limits_{\rho\rightarrow 0}\delta_{\rho}=0$.

results.title: Plurisubharmonic functions and positive currents of type (1,1) over almost complex manifolds
results.theorem:
(Demailly)
Soit $(X,J,\omega)$ une variété complexe hermitienne telle que

$G^{\perp_{\alpha}}_{\omega}(T_{X,J})\geq 0$
pour une certaine $\alpha$ et soit $\psi$ une fonction quasi-plurisousharmonique telle que $i\partial_{{}_{J}}\bar{\partial}_{{}_{J}}\psi\geq\gamma$, où $\gamma$ est une $(1,1)$-forme continue. Soit $\operatorname{exph}^{\omega}$ la partie holomorphe sur les fibres du fibré tangent de l’application exponentielle $\operatorname{exp}^{\omega}$.
L’opérateur régularisant



$\psi_{\varepsilon}(x):=\int\limits_{\zeta\in T_{X,x}}\psi\circ\operatorname{exph}^{\omega}_{x}\,(\zeta)\cdot\chi_{\varepsilon}(|\zeta|^{2}_{\omega_{x}})\frac{\omega^{n}_{x,\zeta}}{n!}$



vérifie les propriétées suivantes:

A) la suite de fonctions $(\psi_{\varepsilon})_{\varepsilon>0}\subset{\cal E}(X,\mathbb{R})$ converge ponctuellement de façon décroissante vers $\psi$ lorsque $\varepsilon>0$ tend vers zéro,

B) on a le contrôle
$i\partial_{{}_{J}}\bar{\partial}_{{}_{J}}\psi_{\varepsilon}\geq\gamma-\delta_{\varepsilon}\omega$ sur la perte de positivité, où $(\delta_{\varepsilon})_{\varepsilon>0}\subset(0,+\infty)$ est une famille de
réels qui tend vers zéro de façon décroissante lorsque $\varepsilon>0$ tend vers zéro.

Un domaine born de $\mathbb{C}^{k}$ bord lisse minimal

results.title: Invariant Kähler potentials and symplectic reduction
results.theorem:
Let $B$ be a complexified $G$-orbit, $\rho$ a $G$-invariant strictly plurisubharmonic function and $p_{0}\in B$ a critical point of $\rho$. If
$\Sigma_{B}$ is a local submanifold transversal to the $G$-orbit $G\cdot p_{0}$ at $p_{0}$ of maximal dimension, then the restriction $\rho|_{\Sigma_{B}}$ has positive Hessian at $p_{0}$ and the $G$-orbit is a local isolated minimum locus
of $\rho$.

results.title: The Minimum Principle for Convex Subequations
results.theorem:
Let $X\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$ be open and $F\subset J^{2,\mathbb{C}}(X)$ be a complex primitive subequation. Suppose



$f:\Omega^{\prime}\to\mathbb{R}$



is such that


(A)

$\Omega^{\prime}\subset X\times\mathbb{C}$ is open, $\mathbb{T}$-invariant and has connected fibres.



(C)

$f$ is $F\#_{\mathbb{C}}\mathcal{P}^{\mathbb{C}}$-subharmonic and $\mathbb{T}$-invariant.



(E)

$f$ attains is fibrewise minimum strictly in the interior.



(F)

$\Omega\subset X\times\mathbb{C}^{*}$.



(H)

$f$ is $\mathcal{C}^{2}$.



Then the marginal function



$g(z):=\inf_{w\in\Omega_{z}}f(z,w)\text{ for }z\in\pi(\Omega)$



is $F$-subharmonic.
